critical_finding.title: CEREVASC OWN PATENT US20160051801A1 ALREADY CLAIMS DUAL PRESSURE+FLOW SENSING ON CSF CATHETER
critical_finding.claim_5_text: The system of claim 1, further comprising at least two transducers positioned on or about the catheter, wherein at least one transducer is a pressure sensor and at least one transducer is a flow sensor.
critical_finding.implication: CereVasc ALREADY has a patent claiming pressure sensing + flow sensing on a CSF catheter. This means RESCUE_001 L1 (CSF pressure sensor) and L6 (monitoring output) are ALREADY DISCLOSED by CereVasc own patent.

limitation_impact.L1_sensor_CSF_pressure: DISCLOSED by US20160051801A1 claim 5 (pressure sensor on CSF catheter)
limitation_impact.L2_venous_sinus_pressure: NOT_DISCLOSED (pressure sensor is in CSF space, not venous sinus)
limitation_impact.L4_eShunt_context: PARTIALLY — catheter accesses CSF space but specific dural venous sinus deployment not in this claim

second_finding.title: CEREVASC PATENT US20160136398A1 MENTIONS PRESSURE AND DIFFERENTIAL IN CSF-VENOUS CONTEXT
second_finding.relevant_text: Method for treating hydrocephalus using a shunt deployed between CP angle cistern and inferior petrosal sinus (IPS). Claims mention pressure and differential in context of CSF drainage.

limitation_impact.L4_subarachnoid_dural: NOT_FOUND (uses CP angle cistern and IPS, not subarachnoid/dural)

second_finding.caveat: Keyword presence does NOT mean the claims actually disclose differential pressure measurement for monitoring. The claims describe a shunt DEPLOYMENT METHOD, not a monitoring system. The keywords appear in the context of treating normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) — the word "pressure" refers to the disease name, not a sensor.

102_result.rationale: No single reference discloses ALL 6 limitations. However, CereVasc own patent US20160051801A1 claim 5 discloses L1 (CSF pressure sensor) and L6 (monitoring output). The remaining limitations (L2 venous sinus pressure, L3 differential, L5 occlusion prediction) are NOT disclosed in any single CereVasc patent. The 102 SURVIVES but is WEAKENED because 2 of 6 limitations are already in CereVasc own portfolio.

103_result.rationale: CereVasc own patent US20160051801A1 already claims dual pressure+flow sensing on a CSF catheter. Adding a venous sinus pressure sensor and calculating a differential is a PREDICTABLE EXTENSION of this existing claim. A PHOSITA reading US20160051801A1 would be motivated to add a venous pressure sensor (the eShunt already accesses the venous sinus). The differential calculation is a straightforward mathematical operation. The occlusion prediction is the only potentially non-obvious element, but trend detection from pressure data is known in the art.
103_result.motivation: STRONG — CereVasc already has dual sensing on CSF catheter; extending to venous sinus is natural
103_result.expectation_of_success: HIGH — pressure sensors work; differential calculation is trivial math
103_result.technical_effect: WEAK — the differential is a mathematical derivative of two known measurements
103_result.whole_claim: MERE_AGGREGATION — pressure sensor + differential + occlusion algorithm = juxtaposition of known elements
103_result.hindsight_risk: MEDIUM — the combination appears obvious given CereVasc existing dual-sensor patent

algorithm_assessment.question: Is the occlusion-predictive algorithm technically meaningful?
algorithm_assessment.answer: WEAK — the algorithm likely uses trend detection (pressure changes over time). This is a GENERIC signal processing technique. While the SIGNAL (CSF-venous differential) may be novel, the ALGORITHM itself is not. The patentability depends on whether the differential measurement is patentable as a method/apparatus — and CereVasc own US20160051801A1 already claims pressure sensing on the CSF catheter.

final_rationale: RESCUE_001 does NOT survive the V4 hostile search. The critical finding is that CereVasc OWN patent US20160051801A1 (claim 5) already discloses dual pressure+flow sensing on a CSF catheter. Adding a venous sinus pressure sensor and calculating a differential is a PREDICTABLE EXTENSION of this existing claim. The 103 risk is HIGH because: (1) CereVasc already has dual sensing, (2) the eShunt already accesses the venous sinus, (3) differential calculation is trivial math, (4) the occlusion algorithm is generic trend detection. The invention is OBVIOUSNESS_RISK — it may be obvious over CereVasc own prior art. Additionally, US20160136398A1 mentions pressure and differential in the CSF-venous context, further weakening novelty.
recommendation: KILL RESCUE_001. The invention cannot survive 103 over CereVasc own US20160051801A1. A dead invention with documented reason is more valuable than a fake ELITE. The documented reason: CereVasc own patent already claims the core sensing architecture.
